q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Short answer — the premise isn’t supported for the P&L (company) ROAS: P&L net ROAS did not rise. Net profit fell because contribution margin dropped sharply while ad‑spend moved slightly higher.

Key evidence (week comparison: 2026-09-30..2026-10-06 -> 2026-10-07..2026-10-13)
- Measured — Net profit: ₹-35,790 → ₹-61,008 (net profit declined). (diagnose_metric_change)
- Measured — P&L components (previous → current) from the P&L view:
  - P&L net sales: ₹616,957.87 → ₹348,887.17
  - P&L net COGS: ₹231,294.69 → ₹211,098.41
  - P&L ad spend: ₹369,544.83 → ₹375,287.72
  (metrics_query q_59c8a6e7f2e8; currency INR)
- Measured/Derived — Contribution margin (net sales − net COGS) fell substantially (≈ ₹385,663 → ₹137,789), and diagnose_metric_change attributed the net profit decline as:
  - Contribution‑margin decline: effect ≈ ₹-19,475 (77% of the net‑profit change) — Measured (diagnose output)
  - Higher ad spend: effect ≈ ₹-5,743 (23% of the net‑profit change) — Measured (diagnose output)

Interpretation (labels)
- Measured: P&L shows net profit down and contribution margin the main mover.  
- Derived: The drop in contribution margin came from much lower P&L net sales in the event week (despite a small reduction in net COGS); ad spend rose slightly and therefore amplified the profit hit.  
- Hypothesis: If you saw “ROAS rising” in a dashboard it may be a different ROAS (platform/gross ROAS vs P&L net ROAS) or a short-term spike in platform‑reported revenue that isn’t P&L‑net after returns/discounts/COGS.
